title: Depth formula for a flat local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m_R)$ and $(S,\mathfrak m_S)$ be Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] local rings (commutative rings with exactly one maximal ideal) and $\varphi:R\to S$ a ring homomorphism which is local, i.e. $\varphi(\mathfrak m_R)\subseteq\mathfrak m_S$, and flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Let $\mathfrak m_RS$ be the ideal of $S$ generated by $\varphi(\mathfrak m_R)$; then $S/\mathfrak m_RS$ is a Noetherian local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_S/\mathfrak m_RS$ (the closed fibre). Then $\operatorname{depth}(S)=\operatorname{depth}(R)+\operatorname{depth}(S/\mathfrak m_RS)$, where the depth of a local ring is its depth as a module over itself [def-weil-pbc-depth], with values in $\{0,1,2,\dots\}\cup\{\infty\}$ and $a+\infty=\infty$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0337 (lemma-apply-grothendieck, line 46374), the special case M = R, N = S of Lemma Tag 0338 (lemma-apply-grothendieck-module, line 46303; EGA IV 6.3.1). Tags verified in tags/tags: 0337,algebra-lemma-apply-grothendieck; 0338,algebra-lemma-apply-grothendieck-module

proof.text: *Setting and finiteness.* Write $\bar S=S/\mathfrak m_RS$. Since $\varphi$ is local, $\mathfrak m_RS\subseteq\mathfrak m_S$, so by [lem-weil-pbc-quotient-local-structure] $\bar S$ is a nonzero local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_S/\mathfrak m_RS$; it is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-noetherian] ($S\to\bar S$ is surjective, so $\bar S$ is generated by $1$ as an $S$-module). For a nonzero Noetherian local ring $A$, $A$ is a nonzero finite $A$-module whose support is all of $\operatorname{Spec}A$, so [lem-weil-pbc-depth-le-support-dimension] gives $\operatorname{depth}(A)\le\dim A$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], which is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-local-finite-krull-dimension]. Hence $\operatorname{depth}(R)$, $\operatorname{depth}(S)$ and $\operatorname{depth}(\bar S)$ are integers $\ge0$ [def-weil-pbc-depth], and $n:=\operatorname{depth}(R)+\operatorname{depth}(\bar S)$ is an integer $\ge0$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0338 (lemma-apply-grothendieck-module, line 46303), proof ("Denote n the right hand side"; finiteness of depth is Lemma Tag 00LK, lemma-bound-depth, line 17814)

proof.text: *The inductive claim.* For an integer $n\ge0$ let $P(n)$ be: for every flat local homomorphism $\psi:A\to B$ of Noetherian local rings with $\operatorname{depth}(A)+\operatorname{depth}(B/\mathfrak m_AB)=n$, one has $\operatorname{depth}(B)=n$. By step 1 the item is the conjunction of all $P(n)$. We prove $P(0)$ (steps 3-4) and, for $n\ge1$, $P(n-1)\Rightarrow P(n)$ (steps 5-8), writing the step for $\psi=\varphi$, $A=R$, $B=S$. This is the source's induction on $n$ for $M=R$, $N=S$: the modules it passes to, $M\otimes_RN/fN=S/fS$ and $M/fM\otimes_RN=S/fS$, are again rings flat over $R$ resp. $R/fR$, so the induction stays among rings.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0338 (lemma-apply-grothendieck-module, line 46303), proof ("by induction on n")

proof.text: *Depth zero gives an element with annihilator the maximal ideal.* Let $(A,\mathfrak m_A)$ be a nonzero Noetherian local ring with $\operatorname{depth}(A)=0$. Then there is $z\in A$ with $\operatorname{Ann}_A(z)=\{a\in A:az=0\}=\mathfrak m_A$. Indeed, otherwise $\mathfrak m_A$ is not an associated prime of the finite $A$-module $A$, and [lem-weil-pbc-nonzerodivisor-if-maximal-not-associated] gives $x\in\mathfrak m_A$ which is a nonzerodivisor on $A$; as $xA\subseteq\mathfrak m_A\neq A$, $A/xA\neq0$, so $x$ is an $A$-regular sequence of length $1$ in $\mathfrak m_A$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence], and $\operatorname{depth}(A)\ge1$ [def-weil-pbc-depth], a contradiction.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0338 (lemma-apply-grothendieck-module, line 46303), proof, first paragraph ("This means there is a z in M whose annihilator is m_R"; Lemma Tag 00LL, lemma-ideal-nonzerodivisor)

proof.text:
*Base case $n=0$.* Then $\operatorname{depth}(R)=0=\operatorname{depth}( ar S)$. By step 3 (for $A=R$ and $A= ar S$) there are $z\in R$ with $\operatorname{Ann}_R(z)=\mathfrak m_R$ and $y\in S$ whose class $ ar y\in ar S$ has $\operatorname{Ann}_{ ar S}( ar y)=\mathfrak m_S/\mathfrak m_RS$. Put $w=\varphi(z)y\in S$. By [lem-weil-pbc-annihilator-element-flat-base-change] ($\varphi$ flat) $\operatorname{Ann}_S(\varphi(z))=\operatorname{Ann}_R(z)S=\mathfrak m_RS$. For $s\in S$: $sw=0\iff sy\in\operatorname{Ann}_S(\varphi(z))=\mathfrak m_RS\iff  ar s ar y=0$ in $ ar S\iff ar s\in\mathfrak m_S/\mathfrak m_RS\iff s\in\mathfrak m_S$ (as $\mathfrak m_RS\subseteq\mathfrak m_S$). So $\operatorname{Ann}_S(w)=\mathfrak m_S
eq S$; hence $w
eq0$ and every $x\in\mathfrak m_S$ kills $w$, so no element of $\mathfrak m_S$ is a nonzerodivisor on $S$. Since $\mathfrak m_SS=\mathfrak m_S
eq S$ and an $S$-regular sequence of length $\ge1$ begins with a nonzerodivisor on $S$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence], the only $S$-regular sequence in $\mathfrak m_S$ is the empty one: $\operatorname{depth}(S)=0=n$ [def-weil-pbc-depth].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0338 (lemma-apply-grothendieck-module, line 46303), proof, first paragraph ("Since N is flat over R the map z: R/m_R -> M produces an injective map N/m_RN -> M tensor N. Hence the annihilator of z tensor y is m_S")

proof.text: *Case $n\ge1$, $\operatorname{depth}(\bar S)\ge1$: the element $f$.* By [def-weil-pbc-depth] ($\mathfrak m_{\bar S}\bar S\neq\bar S$) there is a $\bar S$-regular sequence of length $\ge1$ in $\mathfrak m_S/\mathfrak m_RS$; its first term is the class $\bar f$ of some $f\in\mathfrak m_S$ and is a nonzerodivisor on $\bar S$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-mod-injective] to the local homomorphism $\varphi$ ($S$ Noetherian), the flat $R$-module $M=S$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], the finite $S$-module $N=S$ and the $R$-linear map $u:S\to S$, $s\mapsto fs$: the induced map $\bar u:S/\mathfrak m_RS\to S/\mathfrak m_RS$ is multiplication by $\bar f$, injective. Hence $f$ is a nonzerodivisor on $S$, and $S'=S/fS$ is a flat $R$-module, i.e. the composite $\varphi':R\to S\to S'$ is flat. As $fS\subseteq\mathfrak m_S$, $S'$ is a nonzero local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_S/fS$ [lem-weil-pbc-quotient-local-structure], Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-noetherian], and $\varphi'(\mathfrak m_R)\subseteq\mathfrak m_S/fS$: $\varphi'$ is a flat local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings. Its closed fibre is $S'/\mathfrak m_RS'=S/(fS+\mathfrak m_RS)$, which is also the ring $\bar S/\bar f\bar S$ (both are $S$ modulo the ideal $fS+\mathfrak m_RS$).

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0338 (lemma-apply-grothendieck-module, line 46303), proof, second paragraph ("we may choose f in m_S mapping to a nonzerodivisor on N/m_RN ... According to Lemma 00ME the element f is a nonzerodivisor on N and N/fN is flat over R")

proof.text: *Case $\operatorname{depth}(\bar S)\ge1$: the computation.* (a) By [lem-weil-pbc-depth-drops-by-one] for the Noetherian local ring $\bar S$, the nonzero finite $\bar S$-module $\bar S$ and $\bar f\in\mathfrak m_{\bar S}$: $\operatorname{depth}_{\bar S}(\bar S/\bar f\bar S)=\operatorname{depth}(\bar S)-1$, and by [lem-weil-pbc-depth-over-quotient-ring] (ideal $\bar f\bar S\subseteq\mathfrak m_{\bar S}$) this is the depth of the local ring $\bar S/\bar f\bar S=S'/\mathfrak m_RS'$ (step 5). So $\operatorname{depth}(R)+\operatorname{depth}(S'/\mathfrak m_RS')=n-1$, and $P(n-1)$ for $\varphi':R\to S'$ gives $\operatorname{depth}(S')=n-1$. (b) By [lem-weil-pbc-depth-drops-by-one] for $S$, the module $S\neq0$ and the nonzerodivisor $f\in\mathfrak m_S$ (step 5): $\operatorname{depth}_S(S/fS)=\operatorname{depth}(S)-1$, and by [lem-weil-pbc-depth-over-quotient-ring] (ideal $fS\subseteq\mathfrak m_S$) the left side is $\operatorname{depth}(S')=n-1$. Hence $\operatorname{depth}(S)=n$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0338 (lemma-apply-grothendieck-module, line 46303), proof, second paragraph (Lemma Tag 090R, lemma-depth-drops-by-one, applied twice; the exact sequence 0 -> M tensor N -> M tensor N -> M tensor N/fN -> 0 of Lemma Tag 00HL is, for M = R, the injectivity of f on S from step 5)

proof.text: *Case $n\ge1$, $\operatorname{depth}(\bar S)=0$: the element $f$ and the map $R/fR\to S/fS$.* Then $\operatorname{depth}(R)=n\ge1$, so as in step 5 there is $f\in\mathfrak m_R$ which is a nonzerodivisor on $R$ [def-weil-pbc-depth] [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. By [lem-weil-pbc-annihilator-element-flat-base-change], $\operatorname{Ann}_S(\varphi(f))=\operatorname{Ann}_R(f)S=0$: $\varphi(f)\in\mathfrak m_S$ is a nonzerodivisor on $S$. Put $R'=R/fR$, $S'=S/\varphi(f)S$; by [lem-weil-pbc-quotient-local-structure] and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-noetherian] they are Noetherian local rings with maximal ideals $\mathfrak m_R/fR$, $\mathfrak m_S/\varphi(f)S$, and $\varphi$ induces $\varphi':R'\to S'$, $r\bmod f\mapsto\varphi(r)\bmod\varphi(f)$, which is local. With $J=fR$: $JS=\varphi(f)S$, and by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-module-quotient-flat] $S/JS=S'$ is a flat $R/J$-module for $(r\bmod J)(s\bmod JS)=\varphi(r)s\bmod JS$, which is the module structure given by $\varphi'$; so $\varphi'$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Its closed fibre is $S'/(\mathfrak m_R/fR)S'=S/(\varphi(f)S+\mathfrak m_RS)=S/\mathfrak m_RS=\bar S$, since $\varphi(f)\in\mathfrak m_RS$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0338 (lemma-apply-grothendieck-module, line 46303), proof, third paragraph ("we can choose f in m_R which is a nonzerodivisor on M. As N is flat over R it is also the case that f is a nonzerodivisor on M tensor N"; here M/fM tensor_R N = S/fS)

proof.text: *Case $\operatorname{depth}(\bar S)=0$: the computation.* (a) By [lem-weil-pbc-depth-drops-by-one] for $R$, the module $R\neq0$ and $f$: $\operatorname{depth}_R(R/fR)=\operatorname{depth}(R)-1=n-1$, and by [lem-weil-pbc-depth-over-quotient-ring] (ideal $fR\subseteq\mathfrak m_R$) this is $\operatorname{depth}(R')$. (b) By step 7 $\varphi':R'\to S'$ is a flat local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings with closed fibre $\bar S$, so $\operatorname{depth}(R')+\operatorname{depth}(\bar S)=n-1$ and $P(n-1)$ gives $\operatorname{depth}(S')=n-1$. (c) By [lem-weil-pbc-depth-drops-by-one] for $S$ and the nonzerodivisor $\varphi(f)\in\mathfrak m_S$: $\operatorname{depth}_S(S/\varphi(f)S)=\operatorname{depth}(S)-1$, and by [lem-weil-pbc-depth-over-quotient-ring] the left side is $\operatorname{depth}(S')=n-1$. Hence $\operatorname{depth}(S)=n$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0338 (lemma-apply-grothendieck-module, line 46303), proof, third paragraph ("depth(M tensor N) = depth(M/fM tensor N) + 1 and depth(M) = depth(M/fM) + 1 by Lemma 090R")

proof.text: *Conclusion.* Steps 4-8 prove $P(n)$ for all $n\ge0$ by induction (for $n\ge1$ exactly one of the cases of steps 5-6 and 7-8 applies). By step 1, $n=\operatorname{depth}(R)+\operatorname{depth}(S/\mathfrak m_RS)$ is finite, so $P(n)$ gives $\operatorname{depth}(S)=\operatorname{depth}(R)+\operatorname{depth}(S/\mathfrak m_RS)$. (All three depths are finite, so the convention $a+\infty=\infty$ of the statement is not needed.)
